verdict.rationale: Mixpanel documents JQL, an in-platform custom query language: users write JavaScript with a main() function that its query engine compiles and executes. This is a programmatic, SQL-equivalent way to query data, but it is JavaScript, not SQL. The evidence does not show it running over raw event rows, and the Query API only returns report-style calculated results. missing for 10: actual SQL support, explicit documentation that JQL queries raw events, depth on JQL capabilities and limits, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can query my raw events with SQL (or an SQL-equivalent query language) inside the platform

citations.quote: Create custom queries using Javascript code
The JQL JavaScript code must define a main() function. This JavaScript will be compiled, and the main() function will be executed by the query engine.
